Mhh, I wonder, since we're making a new icon every time anyways, wouldn't it be cleaner to just make it, set it and then destroy it in one go?

It looks like it's not required for the icon object to persist after being set, according to [the documentation](https://wayland.app/protocols/xdg-toplevel-icon-v1#xdg_toplevel_icon_v1:request:destroy):

> Destroys the 'xdg_toplevel_icon_v1' object. The icon must still remain set on every toplevel it was assigned to, until the toplevel icon is reset explicitly.

I haven't tried this approach though (did we already discuss this?), lemme know if you already considered it :D
It's possible to create, set and destroy all in one method. The issue comes because in `WaylandThread::window_create`  we need to have an `xdg_icon` available to set the icon when it's created.
